title: Arica Earthquake and Tsunami
summary: A great offshore earthquake near Arica, then in Peru and now in Chile, struck on 13 August 1868 and sent a tsunami across the Pacific. Waves damaged towns along the Peruvian and Chilean coast and reached the Chatham Islands and New Zealand on 15 August, where they destroyed Tupuangi village.

uncertainty.note: Quake on 13 August local time per Pararas-Carayannis; the tsunami reached New Zealand on 15 August (NZ date per GeoNet).

where.modern_name: Arica, Chile (proxy pin for an offshore epicentre)

importance.justification: Source of the largest recorded distant tsunami to strike New Zealand and an early subject of detailed scientific tsunami analysis.

audience_note: Deaths in the disaster ran to hundreds or thousands; sources disagree on totals.

sources.title: Tsunamis (Peru–Chile tsunami, 1868)

reviewer_note: Pin is Arica city, a proxy; epicentre offshore (~70 km per one source, with an incomplete longitude). Local quake date rests on Pararas-Carayannis, a personal disaster site; magnitude and death tolls vary by source (8.5 to 9.0; 300-350 in Arica vs thousands regionally) so left out.
